title: The True Story of Xuanzang
synopsis: Learn about the real Xuanzang and just how much he differs from the character in Journey to the West.

fullText.simplified:
真实的“唐僧”故事

    说起“唐僧”，中国人的脑海里首先浮现出来的是中国四大名著《西游记》中的唐僧形象。在《西游记》中，唐僧虽然心地善良，却常常人妖不分，还胆小怕事。然而真实的唐僧却与《西游记》中的唐僧形象大相径庭。
    如果要给真实的唐僧贴上标签的话，那他身上有一个非常醒目的标签，那就是“勇敢的探险家”。
    真正的“唐僧”名叫陈祎，法名玄奘。玄奘幼年父母双亡后就在寺庙中长大，十岁出家。他非常聪明，而且喜欢佛法。二十六岁时，玄奘已是精通佛法的高僧了。可是随着他研究的深入，他到达不了更高的境界，也想不通一些高深的问题。
    正在他苦恼的时候，他遇到了一位来自印度的僧人。印度僧人告诉他，他可以去当时的最高佛法学院学习佛法。在学院里有一位得道高僧，可以帮助玄奘解惑。因此玄奘萌生出了西行取经的念头。可当时朝廷因为边境经常受到游牧民族的侵扰，对于出境管控非常严格。玄奘多次申请都被拒绝了。他求法心切，于是决定自己偷渡出境，到佛教起源的印度去寻找真经。
    印度远隔万水千山，玄奘想要去印度，必须要穿越六个国家。在那个时代，交通极其不方便，要徒步从中国到印度是一件无法想象的艰巨的任务。
    玄奘趁夜黑风高，牵着马，带着两个伙伴偷偷摸摸地出发了。走到玉门关附近，他的马倒地累死了，伙伴们受不了苦也逃跑了，只剩下他独自往前走。期间，他翻越过高高的边境守卫城墙，被官兵追赶过，被异教徒追杀过，还因为没有食物而经常挨饿……但他从来没有想过要放弃。
    就这样，他凭着那股常人没有的坚毅，历尽千辛万苦，最终到达了心中所求之地——印度。他在印度拜访了许多有学问的法师，弄清楚了许多问题。十九年后，他带着六百五十七部宝贵的经书回到长安。这时候，官府再也不提他偷渡出境的事情了。唐太宗专门派了一位大臣，把他迎接回长安。当玄奘到来的时候，路边挤满了欢迎的人群。
    后来，玄奘把他在西域的见闻著成了《大唐西域记》。这部书详实地记载了当时西域各国的地理、风土、人情，是后世之人研究中外文化交流、佛教历史、民族史的珍贵资料。
    这就是真实的“唐僧”，他不是《西游记》里那个胆小怕事的僧人，而是一位勇敢的探险家。
fullText.traditional:
真實的“唐僧”故事

    說起“唐僧”，中國人的腦海裡首先浮現出來的是中國四大名著《西遊記》中的唐僧形象。在《西遊記》中，唐僧雖然心地善良，卻常常人妖不分，還膽小怕事。然而真實的唐僧卻與《西遊記》中的唐僧形象大相徑庭。
    如果要給真實的唐僧貼上標籤的話，那他身上有一個非常醒目的標籤，那就是“勇敢的探險家”。
    真正的“唐僧”名叫陳禕，法名玄奘。玄奘幼年父母雙亡後就在寺廟中長大，十歲出家。他非常聰明，而且喜歡佛法。二十六歲時，玄奘已是精通佛法的高僧了。可是隨著他研究的深入，他到達不了更高的境界，也想不通一些高深的問題。
    正在他苦惱的時候，他遇到了一位來自印度的僧人。印度僧人告訴他，他可以去當時的最高佛法學院學習佛法。在學院裡有一位得道高僧，可以幫助玄奘解惑。因此玄奘萌生出了西行取經的念頭。可當時朝廷因為邊境經常受到遊牧民族的侵擾，對於出境管控非常嚴格。玄奘多次申請都被拒絕了。他求法心切，於是決定自己偷渡出境，到佛教起源的印度去尋找真經。
    印度遠隔萬水千山，玄奘想要去印度，必須要穿越六個國家。在那個時代，交通極其不方便，要徒步從中國到印度是一件無法想像的艱巨的任務。
    玄奘趁夜黑風高，牽著馬，帶著兩個伙伴偷偷摸摸地出發了。走到玉門關附近，他的馬倒地累死了，伙伴們受不了苦也逃跑了，只剩下他獨自往前走。期間，他翻越過高高的邊境守衛城牆，被官兵追趕過，被異教徒追殺過，還因為沒有食物而經常挨餓……但他從來沒有想過要放棄。
    就這樣，他憑著那股常人沒有的堅毅，歷盡千辛萬苦，最終到達了心中所求之地——印度。他在印度拜訪了許多有學問的法師，弄清楚了許多問題。十九年後，他帶著六百五十七部寶貴的經書回到長安。這時候，官府再也不提他偷渡出境的事情了。唐太宗專門派了一位大臣，把他迎接回長安。當玄奘到來的時候，路邊擠滿了歡迎的人群。
    後來，玄奘把他在西域的見聞著成了《大唐西域記》。這部書詳實地記載了當時西域各國的地理、風土、人情，是後世之人研究中外文化交流、佛教歷史、民族史的珍貴資料。
    這就是真實的“唐僧”，他不是《西遊記》裡那個膽小怕事的僧人，而是一位勇敢的探險家。

sentences.pinyin: táng tài zōng zhuān mén pài le yí wèi dà chén bǎ tā yíng jiē huí cháng ān
sentences.english: This time, the feudal officials never mentioned his illegal border crossing again.

sentences.simplified: 当玄奘到来的时候，路边挤满了欢迎的人群。
sentences.traditional: 當玄奘到來的時候，路邊擠滿了歡迎的人群。
sentences.pinyin: dāng xuán zàng dào lái de shí hou lù biān jǐ mǎn le huān yíng de rén qún
sentences.english: Emperor Taizong of Tang especially sent a chancellor to welcome him back to Chang’an.
When Xuanzang arrived, the sides of the roads were packed full of people welcoming him.

sentences.simplified: 后来，玄奘把他在西域的见闻著成了《大唐西域记》。
sentences.traditional: 後來，玄奘把他在西域的見聞著成了《大唐西域記》。
sentences.pinyin: hòu lái xuán zàng bǎ tā zài xī yù de jiàn wén zhù chéng le dà táng xī yù jì

sentences.simplified: 这部书详实地记载了当时西域各国的地理、风土、人情，
sentences.traditional: 這部書詳實地記載了當時西域各國的地理、風土、人情，
sentences.pinyin: zhè bù shū xiáng shí de jì zǎi le dāng shí xī yù gè guó de dì lǐ fēng tǔ rén qíng
sentences.english: Later, Xuanzang wrote about his experiences in the Western Regions in the Great Tang Records on the Western Regions.

sentences.simplified: 是后世之人研究中外文化交流、佛教历史、民族史的珍贵资料。
sentences.traditional: 是後世之人研究中外文化交流、佛教歷史、民族史的珍貴資料。
sentences.pinyin: shì hòu shì zhī rén yán jiū zhōng wài wén huà jiāo liú fó jiào lì shǐ mín zú shǐ de zhēn guì zī liào
sentences.english: This book records in detail the geography, local conditions, and social relations of each country in the Western Regions.
It is a precious resource for future generations studying Sino-foreign cultural exchange, Buddhist history, and ethnic history.

sentences.simplified: 这就是真实的“唐僧”，
sentences.traditional: 這就是真實的“唐僧”，
sentences.pinyin: zhè jiù shì zhēn shí de táng sēng

sentences.simplified: 他不是《西游记》里那个胆小怕事的僧人，而是一位勇敢的探险家。
sentences.traditional: 他不是《西遊記》裡那個膽小怕事的僧人，而是一位勇敢的探險家。
sentences.pinyin: tā bú shì xī yóu jì lǐ nà ge dǎn xiǎo pà shì de sēng rén ér shì yí wèi yǒng gǎn de tàn xiǎn jiā
sentences.english: This was the real Xuanzang.
He was not the timid, cowardly monk in Journey to the West; rather, he was a brave and courageous explorer.

raw.synopsis: Learn about the real Xuanzang and just how much he differs from the character in Journey to the West.
sentence_translations: The True Story of Xuanzang
Whenever Xuanzang is mentioned, the first thing that comes into the minds of Chinese people, ..
.. is the image of Xuanzang from Journey to the West, one of the Four Classic Novels of Chinese literature.
In Journey to the West, although Xuanzang is good-natured, ..
.. he often can’t tell good from bad, and is timid and afraid of trouble.
Yet, the real Xuanzang and the image of Xuanzang in Journey to the West are poles apart.
If one was to place a label on the real Xuanzang, ..
.. he would have a very striking label, and that would be “brave explorer”.
The real Xuanzang’s was called Chen Yi and his Dharma name was Xuanzang.
Xuanzang’s parents both died during his childhood, so he grew up in a temple, leaving home to become a monk at age ten.
He was very smart, and liked Buddhist doctrine.
At age twenty-six, Xuanzang was already a senior monk who had mastered the Dharma.
However, as his studies became deeper, ..
.. he was unable to reach higher realms, nor could he get his mind around certain profound issues.
Just as he was vexed about this, he encountered a monk from India.
The Indian monk told him that he could go to the best Dharma School of the time to study the Dharma.
At the school there was a monk who had achieved the Way that could help Xuanzang dispel his doubts.
Thus, the idea of traveling west on a quest for the Buddhist scriptures was planted in Xuanzang’s mind.
But at the time, because the imperial court often faced invasions by nomadic peoples, ..
.. there were very strict controls on leaving the country.
Xuanzang’s multiple applications were all rejected.
He was very eager to seek the Dharma.
So, he decided to illegally cross the border himself to go to India, Buddhism’s place of origin, to seek the true scripture.
It was a long and difficult journey to India. To get to India, Xuanzang had to pass through six countries.
In that era, transportation was extremely inconvenient.
To get from China to India by foot was an unimaginably arduous task.
Xuanzang took advantage of the dark of the night; he lead his horse, took two companions, and set off in secret.
When they neared Yumen Pass, his horse fell over and died of exhaustion.
His companions were unable to bear the hardship and bailed, leaving him continuing on alone.
During this time, he climbed over tall border walls and was chased by officers and men.
He was chased by heathens to be killed, and was often starving due to lack of food … But he never thought of giving up.
Just like this, by virtue of his unmatched perseverance, after experiencing countless hardships and difficulties, ..
.. he finally arrived in the place sought by his heart – India.
In India he paid visits to many knowledgeable Buddhist masters and gained clarity on many issues.
Nineteen years later, he brought 657 volumes of valuable scriptures back to Chang’an.
This time, the feudal officials never mentioned his illegal border crossing again.
Emperor Taizong of Tang especially sent a chancellor to welcome him back to Chang’an.
When Xuanzang arrived, the sides of the roads were packed full of people welcoming him.
Later, Xuanzang wrote about his experiences in the Western Regions in the Great Tang Records on the Western Regions.
This book records in detail the geography, local conditions, and social relations of each country in the Western Regions.
It is a precious resource for future generations studying Sino-foreign cultural exchange, Buddhist history, and ethnic history.
This was the real Xuanzang.
He was not the timid, cowardly monk in Journey to the West; rather, he was a brave and courageous explorer.
